set_title: -itis vs -osis vs -otic: inflammation vs a state or condition
stem: A 70-year-old man on a low-fiber diet passes a large amount of bright red blood per rectum. He has no abdominal pain, fever or change in bowel habit. His abdomen is soft and nontender. His hemoglobin falls from 14 to 11 g/dL, and the bleeding stops by itself. Colonoscopy shows multiple small outpouchings in the sigmoid colon without inflammation.
oneliner: 70M, low-fiber diet + sudden painless bright red blood per rectum + sigmoid outpouchings without inflammation → ?

whyNot.A: Nephrotic syndrome is protein loss in urine; he has **rectal bleeding**
whyNot.B: Diverticulitis is painful and febrile; he has **no pain and no fever**
whyNot.C: Nephritic syndrome is a kidney problem with hematuria; his blood is **rectal and painless**
whyNot.D: Mesenteric ischemia causes severe pain out of proportion; he has **painless bleeding and outpouchings**

why: Many pouches present, without inflammation (-osis, a state). **Painless bright red bleeding from sigmoid outpouchings** is diverticulosis.

idea.rule: -osis = pouches present; -itis = pouches inflamed.
also: False diverticula: mucosa through weak muscle
Most common cause of lower GI bleeding

set_title: -itis vs -osis vs -otic: inflammation vs a state or condition
stem: A 66-year-old woman has had 2 days of left lower abdominal pain, fever and nausea. She has had constipation for years. Temperature is 38.6 C. The left lower quadrant is tender with guarding. Leukocyte count is 15,000/mm3. CT shows thickened sigmoid colon wall with fat stranding around outpouchings.
oneliner: 66F + 2 days of left lower quadrant pain, fever, leukocytosis + CT: inflamed sigmoid with fat stranding → ?

whyNot.A: Diverticulosis is painless pouches; she has **fever, leukocytosis, fat stranding**
whyNot.B: Nephritic syndrome affects the kidney; she has **left lower quadrant pain and fever**
whyNot.D: Nephrotic syndrome shows edema and proteinuria; she has **colonic inflammation on CT**
whyNot.E: Ulcerative colitis causes bloody diarrhea; she has **localized sigmoid inflammation, constipation**

why: Inflamed pouch (-itis, inflammation): a diverticulum has become infected. **Fever, left lower quadrant pain and sigmoid fat stranding** is diverticulitis.

idea.rule: Fever + left lower quadrant pain + leukocytosis = diverticulitis.

set_title: -plasia words: how cells adapt and how they go wrong
stem: A 55-year-old man has had heartburn for 15 years that is partly relieved by antacids. Endoscopy shows salmon-colored mucosa extending 4 cm above the gastroesophageal junction. A biopsy of the distal esophagus shows columnar epithelium with goblet cells in place of the normal squamous lining. There is no cell atypia.
oneliner: 55M + 15 years of reflux + distal esophagus lined by columnar cells with goblet cells + no atypia → ?

whyNot.A: Dysplasia shows disordered, atypical cells; his cells are **mature with no atypia**
whyNot.B: Hyperplasia is more cells; his lining is a **different cell type**
whyNot.D: Anaplasia is loss of differentiation in cancer; his cells are **mature with goblet cells**
whyNot.E: Aplasia is failure of cell formation; he has **replacement by columnar cells**

why: Change to another mature cell type, here from chronic acid injury. **Squamous lining replaced by columnar cells with goblet cells** is metaplasia (Barrett esophagus).

idea.rule: One mature cell type replaced by another = metaplasia; reversible if the cause stops.
also: Barrett can progress to dysplasia and adenocarcinoma

set_title: Cushing names: disease vs syndrome vs ulcer vs reflex (and Curling ulcer)
stem: A 30-year-old man has 50% total body surface area burns after a house fire. On day 3 in the intensive care unit he has black tarry stools and his hemoglobin falls from 13 to 9 g/dL. Endoscopy shows multiple shallow ulcers in the stomach and duodenum. He has no head injury and is not taking anti-inflammatory drugs.
oneliner: 30M, 50% burns, day 3 + melena, falling hemoglobin + shallow gastric and duodenal ulcers → ?

whyNot.A: Cushing ulcer follows brain injury; he has **burns and no head injury**
whyNot.B: Cushing reflex follows raised pressure; he has **melena after burns**
whyNot.D: Cushing disease is a pituitary tumor; he has **stress ulcers after burns**
whyNot.E: Ectopic ACTH is a tumor syndrome; he has **burn-related ulcers**

why: Burn stress ulcer: mucosal ischemia from hypovolemia. **Gastric and duodenal ulcers with bleeding days after severe burns** is a Curling ulcer.

idea.rule: Stress ulcer after burns = Curling; after brain injury = Cushing (vagal acid).

set_title: Chiari names: Chiari I vs Chiari II vs Budd-Chiari vs Dandy-Walker
stem: A 40-year-old woman with polycythemia vera has sudden abdominal pain, rapid weight gain and ascites. The liver is tender and enlarged, ascitic protein exceeds 3 g/dL, and Doppler ultrasonography shows absent hepatic vein flow.
oneliner: 40-year-old woman, polycythemia vera, painful big liver, ascites, absent hepatic vein flow → ?

whyNot.B: A brain disorder; she has **ascites and absent hepatic vein flow**
whyNot.C: A newborn brain disorder; she has **ascites and a painful big liver**
whyNot.D: A posterior fossa malformation; she has **ascites and absent hepatic vein flow**
whyNot.E: A spinal cord cavity; she has **a painful big liver and ascites**

why: George Budd and Hans Chiari described hepatic vein obstruction. **Polycythemia vera, painful hepatomegaly, ascites and absent hepatic vein flow** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: eponym, type I: cerebellar tonsils herniate
eponym, type II: vermis and brainstem herniate
eponym: absent vermis, cystic fourth ventricle

idea.rule: Budd-Chiari = hepatic vein clot; think polycythemia vera, hypercoagulable states.
also: Nutmeg liver; ascites with high protein
Often hypercoagulable states or myeloproliferative disease

set_title: Chole- names: stone, block or infection in the gallbladder vs the duct
stem: A 42-year-old obese woman has had three episodes of right upper quadrant pain after fatty meals, each resolving within 2 hours. She is afebrile and not tender between episodes. Bilirubin, ALP and leukocyte count are normal.
oneliner: 42-year-old obese woman, RUQ pain after fatty meals settling in 2 hours, normal labs → ?

whyNot.A: Pain lasts over 6 hours with fever; hers **resolves in 2 hours**
whyNot.C: Raises bilirubin and ALP; hers are **normal**
whyNot.D: Causes fever, jaundice and pain; she is **afebrile with normal bilirubin**
whyNot.E: Causes itching and high ALP; she has **meal-related pain and normal ALP**

why: Chole (bile) + lith (stone) + -iasis (condition): gallbladder stones. **Fatty-meal colic resolving in hours with normal labs** is symptomatic stones.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Colic after fatty meal, resolves in hours**

idea.rule: Colic under 6 hours = cholelithiasis; over 6 hours with fever = cholecystitis.
also: Cholesterol stones: female, fat, fertile, forty

set_title: Chole- names: stone, block or infection in the gallbladder vs the duct
stem: A 45-year-old woman has had right upper quadrant pain for 10 hours with nausea and temperature 38.4 C. Deep inspiration during palpation of the right upper quadrant stops abruptly from pain. Leukocyte count is 14,000/mm3; bilirubin and ALP are normal.
oneliner: 45-year-old woman, RUQ pain over 10 hours, fever, Murphy sign, normal bilirubin → ?

whyNot.B: Colic resolves in hours without fever; her pain has lasted **10 hours with fever**
whyNot.C: Raises bilirubin and ALP; hers are **normal**
whyNot.D: Needs jaundice and high bilirubin; hers is **normal with a positive Murphy sign**
whyNot.E: Causes itching and high ALP; she has **fever and positive Murphy sign**

why: Chole (bile) + cyst (bladder) + -itis: inflamed gallbladder, usually from a stone in the cystic duct. **Pain over 6 hours, fever and Murphy sign** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Colic after fatty meal, resolves in hours**

idea.rule: Cholecystitis = gallbladder inflammation; normal bilirubin separates it from duct disease.
also: Cystic duct stone; ultrasound: wall thickening

set_title: Chole- names: stone, block or infection in the gallbladder vs the duct
stem: A 70-year-old man has had fever, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain for 2 days, and is now confused with blood pressure 88/50 mm Hg. Bilirubin is 6.5 mg/dL, ALP 420 U/L, and ultrasonography shows a dilated common bile duct.
oneliner: 70-year-old man, fever, jaundice, RUQ pain, confusion, hypotension, dilated bile duct → ?

whyNot.A: Causes colic without fever or jaundice; he has **fever, jaundice and hypotension**
whyNot.B: Causes fever and Murphy sign with normal bilirubin; his bilirubin is **6.5 mg/dL**
whyNot.C: Causes jaundice without systemic infection; he has **fever, confusion and hypotension**
whyNot.E: A chronic itch disease of women; he has **acute fever and shock**

why: Chol- (bile) + angio- (vessel) + -itis: infected, obstructed bile ducts. **Fever, jaundice, right upper quadrant pain, plus confusion and hypotension** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Colic after fatty meal, resolves in hours**

idea.rule: Charcot triad (fever, jaundice, RUQ pain); add confusion and hypotension for Reynolds pentad.

set_title: Chole- names: stone, block or infection in the gallbladder vs the duct
stem: A 35-year-old man with ulcerative colitis has fatigue, itching and ALP 600 U/L. Antimitochondrial antibodies are negative, p-ANCA is positive, and MRCP shows multifocal strictures and dilations of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts.
oneliner: 35-year-old man, ulcerative colitis, high ALP, beaded bile ducts on MRCP → ?

whyNot.A: Causes acute fever and Murphy sign; he has **chronic itch and beaded ducts**
whyNot.C: Shows one obstructing stone; his MRCP shows **multifocal strictures and dilations**
whyNot.D: Causes acute fever and shock; his course is **chronic with ulcerative colitis**
whyNot.E: Affects middle-aged women with antimitochondrial antibodies; his are **negative**

why: Primary: unknown cause; sclerosing: scarring; cholangitis: bile duct inflammation. **Ulcerative colitis, p-ANCA and beaded ducts** point to it.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Colic after fatty meal, resolves in hours**

idea.rule: PSC = men, ulcerative colitis, p-ANCA, beaded ducts; PBC = women, antimitochondrial antibody.

set_title: Surgery endings: -ectomy (cut out), -otomy (cut into), -ostomy (opening), -plasty (repair), -pexy (fix in place), -lysis (break down)
stem: A 4-week-old boy has projectile nonbilious vomiting after every feed and is hungry afterward. An olive-shaped epigastric mass is palpable. Blood gas shows hypochloremic hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis. After fluid and electrolyte correction, which procedure is definitive?
oneliner: 4-week-old boy, projectile nonbilious vomiting, olive mass, alkalosis → which procedure?
ask: Which term names the definitive procedure?

whyNot.A: Removes the gallbladder; he has **an olive mass and projectile vomiting**
whyNot.B: Opens the airway; his problem is **gastric outlet obstruction**
whyNot.C: Repairs the renal pelvis; he has **projectile nonbilious vomiting and an olive mass**
whyNot.D: Fixes the testis in place; he has **projectile vomiting with an olive mass**

why: Pyloro- (pylorus) + myo- (muscle) + -otomy (cut into): cutting the hypertrophied pyloric muscle. **Projectile nonbilious vomiting with an olive mass** is stenosis.

idea.rule: -otomy cuts into without removing; Ramstedt myotomy splits the pyloric muscle.

set_title: Crypto- and cocci- names: Cryptococcus, Cryptosporidium, Coccidioides, Cyclospora
stem: A 30-year-old man with HIV (CD4 count 50/mm3) has 3 weeks of profuse watery diarrhea and cramps, without fever or blood. Modified acid-fast staining of stool shows 4-6 micrometer round oocysts.
oneliner: 30-year-old man, AIDS, chronic watery diarrhea, small acid-fast oocysts → ?

whyNot.A: Causes meningitis in AIDS; he has **watery diarrhea and acid-fast oocysts**
whyNot.B: Causes lung disease in the Southwest; he has **chronic watery diarrhea**
whyNot.C: Oocysts are larger (8-10 micrometers) and follow imported produce; his are **4-6 micrometers**
whyNot.D: Causes lung and marrow disease; he has **watery diarrhea with acid-fast oocysts**

why: Crypto- (hidden) + spore: a hidden spore-forming protozoan. **AIDS with chronic watery diarrhea and small acid-fast oocysts** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Great Lakes; broad-based buds; lung plus skin**

idea.rule: Cryptosporidium = tiny acid-fast oocysts, AIDS or water; Cyclospora = larger, produce.

set_title: -ectasia words: something widened (telangiectasia, duct ectasia, lymphangiectasia)
stem: A 6-year-old girl has had swelling of the legs and face and watery diarrhea for 4 months. Serum albumin and immunoglobulins are low and stool alpha-1 antitrypsin is high. Small-bowel biopsy shows dilated vessels in the villi.
oneliner: 6-year-old girl, edema + diarrhea + low albumin + high stool alpha-1 antitrypsin + dilated villus vessels → ?

whyNot.B: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia bleeds from nose and gut; she has **edema with protein loss**
whyNot.C: Ataxia-telangiectasia needs ataxia and low IgA; she has **edema and high stool alpha-1 antitrypsin**
whyNot.D: Mammary duct ectasia is a breast problem; she has **diarrhea with albumin loss**
whyNot.E: Bronchiectasis is a lung disease; her biopsy shows **dilated villus vessels**

why: Lymph + angi (vessel) + ectasia (widening): gut lymphatics dilate and leak. **Protein-losing enteropathy with dilated villus lymphatics** is intestinal lymphangiectasia.

idea.rule: Lymphangiectasia = widened lymph vessels; the gut leaks protein and lymphocytes.

set_title: Acro- names: things at the ends of the body (hands, feet, face)
stem: An 8-month-old boy who was recently weaned from breast milk has a red, scaly rash around the mouth and anus and on the hands and feet. He has watery diarrhea and thin hair. Serum zinc is low.
oneliner: 8-month-old boy, just weaned + rash around mouth, anus, hands, feet + diarrhea + hair loss + low zinc → ?

whyNot.A: Acromegaly is adult GH excess; he is an **infant with rash and low zinc**
whyNot.B: Acrocyanosis is a harmless color change; he has a **scaly rash and diarrhea**
whyNot.C: Acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans is late Lyme in adults; he has an **infant's rash, diarrhea**
whyNot.D: Acral lentiginous melanoma is an adult cancer; he has an **infant's scaly rash, diarrhea**

why: Acro (extremities) + dermatitis (skin) + enteropathica (gut): zinc malabsorption. **Rash around mouth, anus and limbs with diarrhea after weaning** and low zinc.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **High IGF-1; GH not suppressed by glucose**

idea.rule: Acro- and enteropathica together: skin of the ends plus the gut, from zinc loss.

set_title: Hereditary jaundice names: Gilbert, Crigler-Najjar, Dubin-Johnson, Rotor
stem: A 22-year-old man notices yellow eyes during a 2-day fast before examinations. Total bilirubin is 3.0 mg/dL with direct bilirubin 0.3 mg/dL. Liver enzymes, hemoglobin and blood smear are normal.
oneliner: 22-year-old man, yellow eyes when fasting + bilirubin 3.0, direct 0.3 + normal liver tests and smear → ?

whyNot.A: Crigler-Najjar type 1 is severe and neonatal; he has **mild jaundice, age 22**
whyNot.B: Dubin-Johnson gives conjugated jaundice; his is **mostly unconjugated (direct 0.3)**
whyNot.C: Rotor syndrome gives conjugated jaundice; his is **unconjugated (direct 0.3)**
whyNot.E: Physiologic neonatal jaundice occurs in the first week; he is **22 years old**

why: Mildly reduced UGT activity: unconjugated bilirubin rises with fasting, stress or illness. **Mild indirect hyperbilirubinemia with fasting and normal liver tests** is Gilbert.

idea.rule: Gilbert: benign, mild, indirect, fasting-triggered; no treatment needed.

set_title: Hereditary jaundice names: Gilbert, Crigler-Najjar, Dubin-Johnson, Rotor
stem: A 2-day-old boy has deepening jaundice. Total bilirubin is 28 mg/dL, almost all unconjugated. Hemoglobin is normal and the Coombs test is negative. Phenobarbital does not lower the bilirubin. He becomes lethargic with an arched back.
oneliner: 2-day-old boy, bilirubin 28 unconjugated + no hemolysis + no response to phenobarbital + lethargy and arching → ?

whyNot.A: Hemolytic disease of the newborn causes hemolysis; his **hemoglobin is normal, Coombs negative**
whyNot.C: Dubin-Johnson gives conjugated jaundice; his bilirubin is **almost all unconjugated**
whyNot.D: Rotor syndrome gives conjugated jaundice; his bilirubin is **almost all unconjugated**
whyNot.E: Physiologic jaundice stays mild; his level of **28 mg/dL with arching** signals kernicterus

why: Crigler-Najjar type 1: UGT completely absent, so unconjugated bilirubin rises to toxic levels. **No response to phenobarbital, kernicterus signs at bilirubin 28** fit.

idea.rule: Crigler-Najjar 1: no UGT, no response to phenobarbital; type 2 responds.

set_title: Hereditary jaundice names: Gilbert, Crigler-Najjar, Dubin-Johnson, Rotor
stem: A 25-year-old woman has had mild intermittent jaundice since she started oral contraceptives. Bilirubin is mostly conjugated with normal alkaline phosphatase. At laparoscopy the liver looks black, and biopsy shows dark brown pigment.
oneliner: 25-year-old woman, intermittent jaundice on OCPs + conjugated bilirubin + black liver with pigment → ?

whyNot.A: Gilbert syndrome is unconjugated; her bilirubin is **mostly conjugated with a black liver**
whyNot.B: Crigler-Najjar type 1 is unconjugated and neonatal; she has **conjugated jaundice at 25**
whyNot.C: Rotor syndrome has a normal-colored liver; hers is **black with dark pigment**
whyNot.E: Physiologic jaundice is a newborn finding; she is **25 with conjugated bilirubin**

why: Dubin-Johnson: defective MRP2 excretion of conjugated bilirubin, causing pigment build-up. **Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with a black liver** (versus normal liver in Rotor).

idea.rule: Dubin-Johnson: black liver; Rotor: normal liver. Both conjugated and benign.

set_title: Hereditary jaundice names: Gilbert, Crigler-Najjar, Dubin-Johnson, Rotor
stem: A 3-day-old full-term boy appears healthy and feeds well. Yellow skin of the face and chest began on day 2. Bilirubin is 9 mg/dL, all unconjugated. Hemoglobin is normal, and the Coombs test is negative.
oneliner: 3-day-old full-term boy, well + jaundice from day 2 + bilirubin 9 unconjugated + no hemolysis → ?

whyNot.A: Gilbert syndrome presents later with fasting; he is **3 days old and thriving**
whyNot.B: Crigler-Najjar type 1 gives a much higher level; his **bilirubin of 9 is mild**
whyNot.D: Dubin-Johnson is conjugated; his bilirubin is **all unconjugated**
whyNot.E: Rotor syndrome is conjugated; his bilirubin is **all unconjugated**

why: Immature UGT plus a heavy red-cell load raise indirect bilirubin on day 2-3. **A well, full-term baby with mild jaundice from day 2** and negative Coombs is physiologic.

idea.rule: Physiologic jaundice: day 2-3, mild; jaundice in the first 24 hours is pathologic.

set_title: Esophagus eponyms: Mallory-Weiss, Boerhaave, Barrett, Zenker, Plummer-Vinson
stem: A 40-year-old man has bright-red vomit after an evening of binge drinking and repeated retching. Blood pressure is normal. He has no chest pain and no crepitus. Endoscopy shows a longitudinal mucosal tear at the gastroesophageal junction.
oneliner: 40-year-old man, binge drinking + retching then bright-red vomit + no chest pain + mucosal tear at GE junction → ?

whyNot.A: Boerhaave is a full-thickness rupture with pain and crepitus; he has **no chest pain**
whyNot.B: Barrett esophagus is chronic reflux metaplasia and rarely bleeds; he has an **acute tear**
whyNot.C: Zenker diverticulum causes regurgitation and halitosis; he has **bright-red vomit after retching**
whyNot.E: Plummer-Vinson syndrome causes dysphagia with a web and iron deficiency; he has **bright-red vomit**

why: Longitudinal mucosal tear from forceful retching, usually after alcohol; not through the wall. **Hematemesis after retching without chest pain** is Mallory-Weiss.

idea.rule: Mallory-Weiss = partial tear, bleeds; Boerhaave = full rupture, mediastinitis.

set_title: Esophagus eponyms: Mallory-Weiss, Boerhaave, Barrett, Zenker, Plummer-Vinson
stem: A 50-year-old man develops severe chest pain after forceful vomiting at a banquet. He has fever, crepitus in the neck, and a left pleural effusion. Contrast swallow shows leakage into the mediastinum.
oneliner: 50-year-old man, severe chest pain after forceful vomiting + fever + neck crepitus + contrast leak to mediastinum → ?

whyNot.A: Mallory-Weiss is a mucosal tear that bleeds; he has **chest pain, crepitus, contrast leak**
whyNot.B: Barrett esophagus is chronic metaplasia; he has **an acute rupture with mediastinal leak**
whyNot.C: Zenker diverticulum causes regurgitation of old food; he has **acute pain and crepitus**
whyNot.E: Plummer-Vinson causes dysphagia from a web; he has **an acute rupture with fever**

why: Full-thickness rupture of the distal esophagus from a sudden pressure rise during vomiting. **Chest pain, crepitus and mediastinal contrast leak after vomiting**; surgical emergency.

idea.rule: Boerhaave = full-thickness rupture; mediastinal air gives Hamman crunch.
also: Left pleural effusion with high amylase

set_title: Esophagus eponyms: Mallory-Weiss, Boerhaave, Barrett, Zenker, Plummer-Vinson
stem: A 75-year-old man has had 6 months of bad breath, regurgitation of undigested food hours after eating, and a gurgling sound in his neck when he swallows. Barium swallow shows a posterior pouch above the cricopharyngeus.
oneliner: 75-year-old man, bad breath + regurgitates old food + neck gurgle + posterior pouch above cricopharyngeus → ?

whyNot.B: Mallory-Weiss presents with hematemesis after retching; he has **regurgitation of old food**
whyNot.C: Boerhaave syndrome is an acute rupture; his course is **6 months of regurgitation**
whyNot.D: Barrett esophagus has no pouch; he has a **posterior pouch above the cricopharyngeus**
whyNot.E: Plummer-Vinson has iron deficiency and a web; he has **a pouch and regurgitation**

why: False pulsion pouch through Killian triangle, above a tight cricopharyngeus. **Halitosis, regurgitation of undigested food and a neck gurgle** in an older man.

idea.rule: Zenker: upper, false, above cricopharyngeus; Killian triangle is the weak spot.

set_title: Erythema names: six red rashes with very different causes
stem: A 26-year-old woman with Crohn disease has had tender red lumps on both shins for 1 week. They are painful to touch and are not ulcerated. Biopsy shows inflammation of the fat septa.
oneliner: 26-year-old woman, Crohn disease + tender red shin lumps + septal fat inflammation on biopsy → ?

whyNot.A: Erythema migrans is a single expanding ring; she has **tender lumps on both shins**
whyNot.B: Erythema multiforme has target lesions on palms; she has **tender shin lumps**
whyNot.C: Erythema marginatum is a transient trunk rash; she has **persistent tender shin lumps**
whyNot.D: Erythema infectiosum is a childhood cheek rash; she has **tender shin lumps**

why: Nodosum = knotty: septal panniculitis of the shins. **Tender red shin lumps with Crohn disease**; other triggers are sarcoidosis, strep, TB and pregnancy.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Evanescent pink rings on trunk; rheumatic fever**
**Slapped cheeks, then lacy limb rash; parvovirus**

idea.rule: Nodosum = nodules on the shins; find the trigger: IBD, sarcoid, strep.

set_title: R- eponyms: Reye, Rett, Reiter, Riedel, Richter, Raynaud
stem: A 7-year-old boy has had 3 days of vomiting and then a generalized seizure, and is now drowsy. A week ago he had chickenpox and was given aspirin for fever. He has an enlarged liver without jaundice. Serum ammonia and AST are high, and glucose is low.
oneliner: 7M, aspirin for chickenpox last week + vomiting, seizure, big liver, high ammonia → ?

whyNot.A: Rett syndrome is a girl's regression; he is **a boy with acute liver injury**
whyNot.B: Riedel thyroiditis is a hard neck mass; he has **no neck findings**
whyNot.C: Richter transformation needs CLL; he has **no leukemia, only aspirin exposure**
whyNot.D: Raynaud phenomenon is finger vasospasm; he has **seizure, high ammonia**

why: Named for Reye. Aspirin during a viral illness injures mitochondria: **fatty liver, high ammonia and encephalopathy in a child**.

idea.rule: Reye = child + aspirin + virus; liver and brain fail.
also: Avoid aspirin in viral illness under 19

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **CLL with sudden node growth, high LDH**
**Fingers white, blue, then red in cold**

set_title: Fetal remnant ligament names: arteriosum vs venosum vs teres vs medial vs median
stem: A 58-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis has ascites and dilated veins radiating from his navel. A venous hum is heard at the umbilicus. Portal pressure is high, and flow is moving from the liver toward the abdominal wall veins.
oneliner: 58M, cirrhosis + dilated veins radiating from navel (caput medusae), portal hypertension → remnant they run along → ?
ask: Along which fetal remnant do these portosystemic veins run?

whyNot.A: Medial umbilical ligaments are artery remnants; his veins carry **portal blood to the wall**
whyNot.C: Ligamentum venosum is in the liver fissure; his veins **radiate from the navel**
whyNot.D: Fossa ovalis is in the atrium; his veins are **at the abdominal wall**
whyNot.E: Ligamentum arteriosum is in the chest; his findings are **at the navel**

why: The umbilical vein becomes this ligament in the falciform edge. **Paraumbilical veins along it dilate in portal hypertension** (caput medusae).

idea.rule: Ligamentum teres = old umbilical vein; paraumbilical veins run along it.
also: Paraumbilical veins connect portal and systemic flow

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **In falciform ligament; paraumbilical veins: caput medusae**

set_title: Dys- and odyno- words: swallowing vs speaking vs voice
stem: A 40-year-old woman has had 8 months of food sticking in her chest with both solids and liquids from the start. She regurgitates undigested food at night and has lost weight. A barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus tapering to a bird's beak. Eating causes no pain.
oneliner: 40F, solids and liquids stick from the start + bird's beak on barium, no pain → ?

whyNot.A: Dysphonia is a hoarse voice; her voice is **unaffected, food sticks**
whyNot.B: Odynophagia is painful swallowing; she has **no pain on swallowing**
whyNot.D: Dysarthria is slurred speech; her **speech is clear**
whyNot.E: Dysphasia is a language disorder; her **speech is normal**

why: Dys = difficult, phag = eat. Trouble getting food down: **solids and liquids sticking from the start** suggests a motility disorder.

idea.rule: Dysphagia = difficulty swallowing; odynophagia = pain on swallowing.
also: Both solids and liquids suggests achalasia
Solids only suggests a stricture or ring

set_title: Hemo-/hemat- names: which body part is bleeding or storing iron
stem: A 52-year-old man has fatigue, joint pain in the second and third metacarpophalangeal joints and new diabetes. His skin is bronze. The liver is enlarged. Transferrin saturation is 85% and ferritin is 2,000 ng/mL. Biopsy shows iron in hepatocytes with cirrhosis.
oneliner: 52M, bronze skin + diabetes, MCP arthritis, transferrin saturation 85%, iron-laden cirrhosis → ?

whyNot.A: Hemosiderosis stores iron without organ damage; he has **diabetes, cirrhosis and bronze skin**
whyNot.B: Hemophagocytic syndrome has fever and cytopenias; he has **bronze skin, hepatocyte iron**
whyNot.D: Melena is black stool; he has **no gastrointestinal bleeding**
whyNot.E: Hematochezia is bright red blood per rectum; he has **iron overload**

why: Chroma = color. Iron colors the organs: **bronze skin, diabetes, cirrhosis and arthritis** with high transferrin saturation (HFE C282Y).

idea.rule: Hemochromatosis = iron damages organs; hemosiderosis = iron stored harmlessly.

set_title: Hemo-/hemat- names: which body part is bleeding or storing iron
stem: A 60-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis suddenly vomits a large amount of bright red blood and becomes lightheaded. Blood pressure is 85/50 mm Hg and heart rate is 120/min. He has ascites and spider angiomata. Endoscopy shows bleeding from the distal esophagus.
oneliner: 60M, cirrhosis + sudden large vomit of bright red blood, shock, bleeding esophagus → ?

whyNot.B: Hemoptysis is blood coughed from the lungs; he **vomits bright red blood**
whyNot.C: Melena is black tarry stool; he **vomits fresh blood**
whyNot.D: Hemosiderosis is iron storage; he has **active bleeding from the esophagus**
whyNot.E: Hematochezia is blood passed per rectum; his blood comes **up, from the esophagus**

why: Emesis = vomiting. Blood from above the ligament of Treitz brought up: **bright red vomit from esophageal varices** in cirrhosis.

idea.rule: Hematemesis = blood up from the gut; hemoptysis = blood up from the lungs.

set_title: Hemo-/hemat- names: which body part is bleeding or storing iron
stem: A 48-year-old woman takes ibuprofen daily for arthritis. For 2 days she has had black, sticky, foul-smelling stools. She has epigastric pain but has not vomited. She is pale with heart rate 105/min. Rectal exam shows black stool and no bright red blood.
oneliner: 48F, daily NSAID + 2 days of black sticky foul stools, epigastric pain → ?

whyNot.A: Hematemesis is vomited blood; she **has not vomited**
whyNot.B: Hemosiderosis is iron storage without bleeding; she has **black stools and pallor**
whyNot.C: Hematochezia is bright red blood per rectum; her stool is **black and sticky**
whyNot.E: Hemoptysis is blood coughed up; she has **black stools**

why: Melaina = black. Blood digested by acid and bacteria: **black tarry stool after NSAIDs** points to an upper gastrointestinal source such as an ulcer.

idea.rule: Melena = black tarry stool, upper GI bleed; hematochezia = red, lower GI.
also: Needs about 50 to 100 mL of blood
Bismuth and iron also darken stool

set_title: Charcot names: one neurologist, five unrelated findings
stem: A 60-year-old woman with known gallstones has 2 days of fever to 39.5 C, yellow eyes and pain in the right upper abdomen. Bilirubin is 5 mg/dL with alkaline phosphatase 400 U/L. Ultrasound shows a dilated common bile duct with a stone.
oneliner: 60F, gallstones + fever, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain, dilated duct → ?
ask: Which term names this set of findings?

whyNot.A: Charcot-Leyden crystals are asthma sputum crystals; she has **fever, jaundice, RUQ pain**
whyNot.C: Charcot-Marie-Tooth is an inherited neuropathy; she has **a bile duct stone**
whyNot.D: Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysm is a brain vessel lesion; she has **fever and jaundice**
whyNot.E: Charcot joint is a painless destroyed joint; she has **fever, jaundice, RUQ pain**

why: Three signs together: **fever, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain** mark ascending cholangitis; add shock and confusion for Reynolds pentad.

idea.rule: Charcot triad = fever, jaundice, RUQ pain; Reynolds adds shock, confusion.
also: Treat with antibiotics and biliary drainage
